title: Visual update 2 weeks later
author: Axel0009
selftext:
Here’s what’s changed over the past two weeks. The main feedback on my first post was that it was hard to tell what was on screen and some areas were too dark. I’ve tried to keep the same look while making things easier to see. I also swapped out a few assets, which are still a work in progress.

I originally planned to add some classic horror game elements. I ended up focusing entirely on the story, so it’s turned into a walking simulator with a dark story.

For the assets, I’ve just been using Astra hooked up to Blender. The biggest improvement came when I asked the AI to always look for visual references from both similar-looking games and real life, even when I didn’t give it any myself. The rest has been me playing the game, spotting issues, and writing prompts to fix them. That includes lighting, asset placement, and bugs like objects clipping through each other.

comments.author: suspicious-jabroni
comments.body: How did you ask Astra to do the assets? Wondering what the workflow looks like, also got mine hooked up to blender. Not sure how to keep things consistent on what I’m doing

replies.author: Axel0009
replies.body: Nothing special. I gave Astra some screenshots from games with the look I wanted and asked it to create an art bible explaining how to get that same look. For each new asset, I ask it to look up real-life photos and references from other games, then use the art bible to keep the style consistent. After that, I just ask for a few small changes here and there until it looks right to me. Honestly, a lot of the vibe comes from the lighting and dithering once everything’s in the scene.
